rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw is a one-cycle low pulse
rules.statement: A one-cycle low pulse on i_rst_n_sw must be captured by the write FSM at the first write edge where it is 0, and the reset sequence must complete.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw stays low for a long time
rules.statement: While i_rst_n_sw stays low, the write FSM waits in HOLD and writes stay blocked, while the read side is released.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while write FSM is in REL
rules.statement: Writes stay blocked and a new sequence starts when the FSM is back in RUN; o_sw_rst_busy falls for one cycle between the two sequences.

rules.condition: A read occurs between the assertion of i_rst_n_sw and the arrival of the request at the read side
rules.statement: The read is accepted as a normal read of pre-reset data, and the word is discarded by the reset.

rules.condition: A write occurs in the same edge in which i_rst_n_sw falls
rules.statement: The write must be rejected because the write block is combinational from i_rst_n_sw.

rules.condition: Read or write attempted during the software reset
rules.statement: The access must be rejected without an error pulse; a read of the empty FIFO right after the read release gives a normal underflow pulse.
Storage content is not cleared by the software reset; o_rd_data shows the word at address 0 while the FIFO is empty.

rules.condition: Hardware reset occurs during the software reset
rules.statement: Hardware reset has priority over the software reset; a reset of both domains gives a clean restart.

rules.condition: A clock stops during the software reset
rules.statement: The handshake waits until the clock runs again.
The four-phase handshake is level based so longer delay only lengthens the sequence, and the multi-bit pointers are protected by the flush check.
Threshold flags show empty-FIFO values: o_full_thr = 0 for i_full_thr > 0 and o_empty_thr = 1.
o_sw_rst_busy equals 'write FSM not in RUN' at every write-clock edge.
No write is accepted while wr_blk is active.
No read is accepted while rd_blk is active.
o_full is 1 and o_full_thr has the value of an empty FIFO while the write side is blocked.
o_empty is 1 and o_empty_thr is 1 while the read side is blocked.
No read returns a word that was never written, and data of every accepted read equals the written word.

rules.condition: At each release of a side
rules.statement: At each release the own pointer and the synchronized pointer of the other side are 0.
The read release is before the write release and after the request; o_empty = 1 while both pointers are 0 after the read release.
Both FSMs are in RUN, both pointers are 0, o_empty = 1 and o_full = 0.
The reset sequence must not deadlock; a timeout must detect a deadlock.
o_sw_rst_busy is driven directly by flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy, changes only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr and never glitches.

rules.condition: Write FSM states RUN, REQ, PTR, HOLD, REL
rules.statement: o_sw_rst_busy is 0 in RUN and 1 in REQ, PTR, HOLD and REL; FSM follows RUN, REQ, PTR, HOLD, REL, RUN with stated entry conditions and req_wr set in REQ.
wr_blk follows i_rst_n_sw in the same cycle; o_sw_rst_busy rises at the first write-clock edge after i_rst_n_sw falls.
o_sw_rst_busy rises at the same edge as req_wr.
o_sw_rst_busy stays 1 when i_rst_n_sw returns to 1 (HOLD, REL).
o_sw_rst_busy does not follow the read FSM; it falls only when the write side is released, after the read side.
o_sw_rst_busy, wr_blk and o_full fall at the same edge where the write FSM returns to RUN.
wr_blk equals o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0).

rules.condition: Hardware reset of the write domain, any sequence state
rules.statement: A hardware reset of the write domain clears o_sw_rst_busy asynchronously.
o_sw_rst_busy falls for exactly one write-clock cycle between the two sequences, and writes stay blocked during the gap.
o_sw_rst_busy falls at the edge where the write FSM returns to RUN, together with wr_blk and o_full.

rules.condition: Consumer in the read domain needs o_sw_rst_busy
rules.statement: A read-domain consumer needing o_sw_rst_busy shall synchronize it itself, or use o_empty, since the IP has no synchronizer for it.
